userStories.title: Fold the removed permission keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fold five duplicate permission keys into their surviving keys atomically with their route consumers, closing Project Admin access to global agent updates.

**Motivation** — One of them lets a Project Admin edit an agent's global record (review finding A/SEC-2).

**Approach** — All in `apps/api/src/permissions/catalog.ts` and the `proposed_key` / `catalog_scope` columns of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-action-inventory.tsv`, whose rows `catalog.spec.ts` re-reads:

| TSV row (route) | Baseline `proposed_key` / `catalog_scope` | Target |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `PATCH /agents/:slug/update-roles` | `agent.roles.update` / `global` | `agent.update` / `global` |
| `PATCH /projects/:slug/members/:userId` | `member.role.update` / `project` | `role.binding.manage` / `project` |
| `POST /projects/:slug/agents` | `project.agent.add` / `project` | `member.add` / `project` |
| `DELETE /projects/:slug/agents/:agentSlug` | `project.agent.remove` / `project` | `member.remove` / `project` |
| `PATCH /projects/:slug/agents/:agentSlug` | `project.agent.update` / `project` | `agent.update` / `global` |

- `role.binding.manage` now has an inventory row, so it moves out of `NEW_KEY_SCOPES` and into `INVENTORY_SCOPE_ROWS` (scope `project`). It must not appear in both: `CATALOG_KEYS` concatenates them, and the catalog must hold no duplicate.
- The catalog goes from 226 to 221 keys.
- `agent.update` keeps scope `global`: every row naming it is `global`.
- Seeded role contents are unchanged:
  - Project Admin's `*` covers `member.add`, `member.remove` and `role.binding.manage`, just as it covered the folded keys.
  - `agent.update` stays with global Owner and Admin.
  - No seeded role names a folded key explicitly.
- `ProjectsController.updateProjectAgent` asks `permissions.can(principal, 'agent.update')` (two arguments, no context), in place of `can(principal, 'project.agent.update', { projectId })`. Its parameter list is unchanged: `@CurrentProject() ctx` stays, so the existing unit cases keep calling it with five arguments. The self-update rule (`isAgentPrincipal(principal) && principal.slug === agentSlug`) and the roster lookup are unchanged.
- The `@ApiOperation` / `@ApiResponse` texts of the five routes name the new keys, and `openapi.json` is regenerated with `bun run api:export-spec`.

Binding ruling: **`project.agent.update` folds into the global `agent.update` now**, per the design. A Project Admin is refused `PATCH /projects/:slug/agents/:agentSlug` with 403 `permissions`. A global Owner or Admin may still update a rostered agent, and an agent may still update itself (graceful OFFLINE). Enforce-core's AC-17 ("a project-admin binding alone updates a rostered agent's status") is inverted.

Regression edits travel with the implementation: remove role.binding.manage from catalog.spec.ts's copied NEW_KEY_SCOPES; its former five-agent-management-key invariant now pins the four surviving global keys. Update projects.controller.spec.ts's route table to member.add/member.remove/agent.update and its can assertions to exactly two arguments, leaving five-argument handler calls and self-update/roster-404/refusal cases unchanged; rename the project-admin allow unit case to a caller holding agent.update. Update project-members.controller.spec.ts's updateRole row to role.binding.manage, retaining other rows. In core-project-routes.integration.spec.ts invert AC-17 to 403 permissions and ACTIVE unchanged, retain AC-15 self-update and AC-16 peer refusal, and rename folded-key comments. In core-members-invites.integration.spec.ts the PATCH/DELETE comment becomes role.binding.manage/member.remove with all cases unchanged. Preserve core-agent-routes allow/refuse anchors. Regenerated openapi.json changes only these five operations' summaries/403 descriptions, not paths or schemas. Only existing e2e cases broken by this correct fold are edited; no unrelated new endpoint e2e cases.

Fixture wording: a user whose only source in p1 is a project-admin binding has no ProjectMember row and no global admin role; a global admin has a global admin binding; a rostered agent has a viewer binding in p1. Reset then boot the app, or explicitly run SystemRoleSeeder.onApplicationBootstrap() after resetDb. Refusal is new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'permissions').

**Scope** — In: the catalog/TSV fold, five route declarations and texts, exact global can call, affected existing regressions and root OpenAPI regeneration. Out: runner and remaining route declarations (US-002/003), system-writer metadata (US-004), matrix/checker/collector (US-005/006/007), seeded-role changes and legacy mechanism deletion.
- Rewriting the stored permissions of an existing database's unlocked system roles or custom roles that name a folded key is out of scope: koda-wk is reset by decision 2, and `SystemRoleSeeder` re-seeds system roles.
- Replacing `PATCH /projects/:slug/agents/:agentSlug` with the binding routes, and the web pages for roles, bindings and the merged member list, are out of scope (`permissions-p1-web`).
- Regenerating the CLI client (`apps/cli/src/generated/`) is out of scope; only `openapi.json` is regenerated, and only route descriptions change.

**Interface** — `permissions.can(principal, 'agent.update')` (two arguments, no context). `ProjectsController.updateProjectAgent` retains `@CurrentProject() ctx` and its existing five-argument parameter list.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] The set of PERMISSION_CATALOG keys and the set { project.agent.add, project.agent.remove, project.agent.update, member.role.update, agent.roles.update } have no key in common.
[unit] PERMISSION_CATALOG holds exactly one entry with key role.binding.manage, and its scope is 'project'.
[unit] findCatalogEntry('agent.update') returns an entry with scope 'global'.
[unit] expandEntries of the seeded project-admin role's permissions with scope 'PROJECT' returns a set containing member.add, member.remove and role.binding.manage.

[unit] Reading REQUIRES_METADATA from ProjectsController.addProjectAgent, ProjectsController.removeProjectAgent, ProjectsController.updateProjectAgent, ProjectMembersController.updateRole and AgentsController.updateRoles returns the handler-to-keys map { addProjectAgent: ['member.add'], removeProjectAgent: ['member.remove'], updateProjectAgent: ['agent.update'], updateRole: ['role.binding.manage'], updateRoles: ['agent.update'] }.
[unit] ProjectsController.updateProjectAgent for a rostered agent, with a PermissionService double, calls can exactly once with exactly the two arguments (principal, 'agent.update').

[integration] Given a user whose only source in p1 is a project-admin binding, PATCH /projects/p1/agents/<slug> with { status: 'OFFLINE' } for a rostered agent returns 403 with error code permissions and leaves the agent's status ACTIVE.
[integration] Given a global admin, PATCH /projects/p1/agents/<slug> with { status: 'OFFLINE' } for a rostered agent returns 200 with the agent's persisted status OFFLINE.
[integration] Given a rostered agent using its own API key, PATCH /projects/p1/agents/<its own slug> with { status: 'OFFLINE' } returns 200.

routing.reasoning: Atomic catalog/route migration across multiple controllers changes an access-control boundary and inverts a DB-backed regression; strict security isolation is required.

modifiedFiles.reason: its `NEW_KEY_SCOPES` copy lists `role.binding.manage`, so with the inventory now naming it, "holds exactly the inventory keys plus the keys the design adds, with no duplicates" would expect it twice. Separately, "US-001 AC-13: the five agent-management keys are scoped globally" lists `agent.roles.update`. The replacing invariant: `NEW_KEY_SCOPES` no longer holds `role.binding.manage`, which is derived from its inventory row with scope `project`; AC-13 checks the four remaining agent-management keys; every other derivation is unchanged.

its table of migrated routes pins `['addProjectAgent', ['project.agent.add'], 'guard']`, `['removeProjectAgent', ['project.agent.remove'], 'guard']` and `['updateProjectAgent', ['project.agent.update'], 'service']`. Its `updateProjectAgent` cases assert `permissions.can` was called with `(principal, 'project.agent.update', { projectId: 'proj-1' })`. The replacing invariant: the table pins `member.add` (guard), `member.remove` (guard) and `agent.update` (service); the cases assert `can` was called with exactly `(principal, 'agent.update')`; the handler is still called with five arguments; the self-update, roster 404 and refusal outcomes are unchanged. The case titled "a project admin (global MEMBER with a project-admin binding) is admitted by its can answer" is renamed to say the caller holds `agent.update`.
its route table pins `['updateRole', 'member.role.update']`. The replacing invariant: `updateRole` declares `role.binding.manage`; the other rows are unchanged.

"AC-17: a project-admin binding alone updates a rostered agent's status with 200" expects 200 for the `padmin` user. The replacing invariant (ruling 2026-10-21): that user gets 403 with error code `permissions` and the agent's status stays `ACTIVE`; AC-15 (self-update) and AC-16 (peer refused) are unchanged; the comments naming `project.agent.add` / `project.agent.remove` name `member.add` / `member.remove`.

its comment above AC-3 says the PATCH/DELETE member routes "need member.role.update / member.remove". The replacing invariant: the comment names `role.binding.manage` / `member.remove`; every case is unchanged (Project Admin holds both keys, as before).

the five routes' operation summaries and 403 descriptions name the folded keys. The replacing invariant: it is regenerated with `bun run api:export-spec`, and every path and schema other than those texts is unchanged.

userStories.title: Declare runner-route keys and admit runner principals
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Declare the seven runner keys on their six controllers and teach RequiresGuard that only runner principals hold runner-access keys.

**Motivation** — A new route without `@Requires` is silently open to any authenticated principal. No test notices.

**Approach** — Runner rows of the route-declaration design table:

| Route | Key(s) | Enforced by | Notes |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `PUT /fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/bundle` (`BundleUploadController.upload`) | `runner.bundle.upload` | guard | class-level `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)` next to `@RunnerRoute()` |
| `POST /fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/:name` (`RunnerToolController.call`) | `runner.tool.call` | guard | same |
| `PUT /fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/logs/:stream` (`LogUploadController.append`) | `runner.log.append` | guard | same |
| `GET /fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/config-edit` (`RunnerConfigEditController.get`) | `runner.config.read` | guard | same |
| `GET /fleet/runner/me` (`RunnerApiController.me`) | `runner.self.read` | guard | same |
| `POST /fleet/runner/enroll` (`RunnerApiController.enroll`) | `runner.enroll` | service | `@Public()`; `EnrollmentService.enroll` checks the enrollment token |
| `POST /fleet/runner/sync` (`RunnerSyncController.sync`) | `runner.sync` | guard | same as the first row |

### `RequiresGuard`: runner keys

`apps/api/src/permissions/requires.guard.ts`, `passes`:

Target:
```ts
const entry = findCatalogEntry(key);
if (!entry) return false;
if (entry.access === 'public') return true;
// A runner key is held by runner principals only; PermissionService.can never grants one.
if (entry.access === 'runner') return principal?.actorType === 'runner';
if (!principal) return false;
```

`@Requires(keys, { enforcedBy: 'service' })` means the handler, its service or a route-specific guard checks the access, and `RequiresGuard` only records the keys. Every other route this feature touches is guard-enforced: `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)` is in the same class or handler, as `apps/api/src/auth/auth.controller.ts` does it.

**No access changes except the fold.** Declaring a key on the runner, MCP, health, live, roles and memory routes changes no response for any caller. The runner rule (below) admits exactly the principals `CombinedAuthGuard` already admits on a runner route. `mcp.access` and `notification.read` are implicit keys, and `health.read` is public. Only US-001's fold changes who may call a route.

Preserve RequiresGuard's public branch, unknown-key refusal, service pass-through, metadata precedence, modes and ownership handling. PermissionsModule stays global and the guard needs no provider entry. Refused runner keys throw new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'permissions'); requests with a user principal, agent principal or no principal are denied by this guard. CombinedAuthGuard continues to refuse non-runner credentials on runner routes before this guard, as today. POST /fleet/runner/enroll with no principal is passed through by RequiresGuard; EnrollmentService.enroll still decides using the enrollment token.

Mirror the existing Reflector/context/can-double harness in requires.guard.spec.ts. Add a source-level runner-route-declarations.spec.ts for the complete metadata map and class guards, and runner-route-permissions.integration.spec.ts for enrolled runner me/public enrollment outcomes. DB-backed cases reset then boot to seed system roles and must run under test:scoped with Postgres, not skip. The six runner controllers have no unit spec constructing them; their full-app integration tests already resolve global PermissionService. No new unrelated endpoint e2e cases.

**Scope** — In: runner declaration metadata, class guards and the single runner-access branch. Out: catalog fold (US-001), non-runner route declarations (US-003), writer metadata (US-004), matrix/checker/collector (US-005/006/007). US-002 only: changing how `CombinedAuthGuard` authenticates runner keys or fences jobs (`runnerId` + `leaseEpoch`) is out of scope; only the key declaration and the guard's runner rule are added.

**Interface** — Existing `RequiresGuard.canActivate(ctx: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean>` remains unchanged; `passes` short-circuits `entry.access === 'runner'` with `principal?.actorType === 'runner'`. Runner enroll declares `{ keys: ['runner.enroll'], mode: 'all', enforcedBy: 'service' }`; the other six handlers declare `{ keys: [key], mode: 'all', enforcedBy: 'guard' }`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] RequiresGuard.canActivate on a handler decorated @Requires('runner.sync'), for a request whose user is a runner principal, resolves true without calling PermissionService.can.

[unit] RequiresGuard.canActivate on a handler decorated @Requires('runner.sync'), for a request whose user is a user principal, rejects with ForbiddenAppException carrying prefix 'permissions' and httpStatus 403.

[unit] RequiresGuard.canActivate on a handler decorated @Requires('runner.sync'), for a request whose user is an agent principal, rejects with ForbiddenAppException carrying prefix 'permissions' and httpStatus 403.
[unit] RequiresGuard.canActivate on a handler decorated @Requires('runner.sync'), for a request with no user, rejects with ForbiddenAppException carrying prefix 'permissions' and httpStatus 403.

[unit] Reading REQUIRES_METADATA from the seven runner handlers returns the Class.handler map matching the runner design rows: BundleUploadController.upload=runner.bundle.upload, RunnerToolController.call=runner.tool.call, LogUploadController.append=runner.log.append, RunnerConfigEditController.get=runner.config.read, RunnerApiController.me=runner.self.read and RunnerSyncController.sync=runner.sync each as { keys: [key], mode: 'all', enforcedBy: 'guard' }, and RunnerApiController.enroll as { keys: ['runner.enroll'], mode: 'all', enforcedBy: 'service' }.

[unit] Reading class-level GUARDS_METADATA from each of BundleUploadController, RunnerToolController, LogUploadController, RunnerConfigEditController, RunnerApiController and RunnerSyncController includes RequiresGuard.
[integration] In the booted app, GET /fleet/runner/me with an enrolled runner's kr_ key returns 200 with that runner's name.
[integration] In the booted app, POST /fleet/runner/enroll with no Authorization header and a valid unused enrollment token returns 201 with a body whose apiKey starts with kr_.
[unit] RequiresGuard.canActivate on the service-enforced RunnerApiController.enroll handler with no principal resolves true, leaving EnrollmentService.enroll to decide access as today.

routing.reasoning: One explicit runner-access branch and repetitive controller metadata use the existing guard harness and boot helper without new infrastructure; access-control changes still require the security-mandated strict TDD strategy.

userStories.title: Declare MCP, health, live, role and memory route keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Finish non-runner route declarations without changing existing response or service authorization behavior.

**Motivation** — Nothing yet proves it stays that way.

**Approach** — Non-runner rows of the route-declaration design table:

| Route | Key(s) | Enforced by | Notes |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `POST`, `GET`, `DELETE /mcp` (`McpController.post/get/delete`) | `mcp.access` | guard | implicit key; the controller's user refusal is unchanged |
| `GET /health` (`HealthController.check`) | `health.read` | guard | `@Public()` kept, plus `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)` |
| `GET /projects/:slug/threads/:id/events` (`ThreadEventsController.events`) | `thread.read` | service | `ThreadEventsGuard` already checks `thread.read` |
| `GET /threads/:id/events` (`WorkspaceThreadEventsController.events`) | `thread.workspace.read` | service | `WorkspaceThreadEventsGuard` checks the caller owns the thread |
| `GET /projects/:slug/events` (`LiveController.events`) | `project.read` | service | the handler's membership check stays |
| `GET /me/events` (`MeLiveController.events`) | `notification.read` | service | implicit key; the handler's user-only check stays |
| `GET /roles` (`RolesController.list`) | `role.read` | service | `RoleAdminService.assertCan` |
| `POST /roles`, `PATCH /roles/:id`, `DELETE /roles/:id` | `role.manage` | service | same |
| `GET /role-bindings` (`RoleBindingsController.list`) | `role.read` | service | same |
| `POST /role-bindings`, `DELETE /role-bindings/:id` | `role.binding.manage`, `role.binding.global`, `role.binding.owner` (mode `any`) | service | `RoleAdminService` picks the key from the binding's scope and role |
| `POST /memory` (`MemoryController.createMemory`) | `memory.create`, `memory.update` | service | unchanged check; `memory.update` is the attribution and replace key the service already asks |
| `POST /memory/decisions` (`MemoryController.recordDecision`) | `memory.decision.record`, `memory.update` | service | same |

`thread.workspace.read`, `project.read` and `notification.read` on the three live streams name the key their access corresponds to. Making those handlers ask `PermissionService.can` for it is out of scope (retire-checks replaces their membership checks).

`@Requires(keys, { enforcedBy: 'service' })` means the handler, its service or a route-specific guard checks the access, and `RequiresGuard` only records the keys. The roles and role-bindings routes, the four live streams and the memory writes use it. Every other route this feature touches is guard-enforced: `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)` is in the same class or handler, as `apps/api/src/auth/auth.controller.ts` does it.

**No access changes except the fold.** Declaring a key on the runner, MCP, health, live, roles and memory routes changes no response for any caller. The runner rule (below) admits exactly the principals `CombinedAuthGuard` already admits on a runner route. `mcp.access` and `notification.read` are implicit keys, and `health.read` is public. Only US-001's fold changes who may call a route.

Add RequiresGuard to MCP and health at class or handler level; default mode is all, except binding writes any. Do not add guards that reinterpret service-enforced declarations as authorization requirements. In particular, memory.update metadata describes existing global attribution and transactional replacement checks, not a new blanket grant required for creates. Keep RoleAdminService's existing scope/role/owner selection and refusal code new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'permissions'). Keep the health public response and stream behavior unchanged. PermissionsModule is global and RequiresGuard needs no provider entry.

Modify `apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/mcp/mcp.controller.routes.spec.ts`: its PermissionService double currently exposes only projectIdsWithKey; add can resolving `{ allowed: true, reason: 'implicit' }`, retaining 409 when MCP is off, 403 for a user, initialize, tools/list and tools/call outcomes. Add remaining-route-declarations.spec.ts for the full 17-handler metadata map and guard metadata, and remaining-route-permissions.integration.spec.ts for health and roles route outcomes. DB tests reset before boot or seed system roles after reset. No new endpoint e2e case for declaration-only changes; only edit existing e2e cases a correct implementation breaks.

**Scope** — In: the fifteen newly declared non-runner handlers plus the two memory write declarations, MCP/health guard registration and the isolated MCP double repair. Out: key folding (US-001), runner behavior (US-002), writers (US-004), matrix/checker/collector (US-005/006/007).
- Making the live-stream handlers (`LiveController`, `MeLiveController`, `WorkspaceThreadEventsGuard`) ask `PermissionService.can` for their declared key in place of their membership, user-only or ownership checks is out of scope (`permissions-p1-retire-checks`).
- Deleting `KodaCaslAbilityFactory`, `@RequiredPermission`, `@ProjectPermission`, `@ProjectRoles`, `exemptAgents`, `canOverrideClose`, `withProjectRole`, `canManageMembers`, `ProjectAccessService.assertProjectMembership` / `assertProjectAdmin`, `AssistantTool.permission` / `ToolPermission`, `TicketTransitionsService.assertTransitionPermission`, `FleetActivityService.memberProjectIds`, the unreachable IN_PROGRESS → VERIFIED transition rule and the i18n messages `skills.principal` / `skills.projectPrincipal` is out of scope (`permissions-p1-retire-checks`).

**Interface** — `@Requires(keys, { enforcedBy: 'service' })`; binding writes use `@Requires(['role.binding.manage', 'role.binding.global', 'role.binding.owner'], { mode: 'any', enforcedBy: 'service' })`. Memory writes declare respectively `['memory.create', 'memory.update']` and `['memory.decision.record', 'memory.update']`, with mode all and service enforcement.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] Reading REQUIRES_METADATA from the fifteen non-runner handlers and MemoryController.createMemory/recordDecision into Class.handler -> { keys, mode, enforcedBy } returns: McpController.post/get/delete each ['mcp.access']/all/guard; HealthController.check ['health.read']/all/guard; ThreadEventsController.events ['thread.read']/all/service; WorkspaceThreadEventsController.events ['thread.workspace.read']/all/service; LiveController.events ['project.read']/all/service; MeLiveController.events ['notification.read']/all/service; RolesController.list ['role.read']/all/service; RolesController.create/update/remove each ['role.manage']/all/service; RoleBindingsController.list ['role.read']/all/service; RoleBindingsController.create/remove each ['role.binding.manage', 'role.binding.global', 'role.binding.owner']/any/service; MemoryController.createMemory ['memory.create', 'memory.update']/all/service; MemoryController.recordDecision ['memory.decision.record', 'memory.update']/all/service.
[unit] Every route declared by McpController and HealthController has RequiresGuard in class-level or handler-level GUARDS_METADATA.
[integration] In the booted app, GET /health with no Authorization header returns 200 with status 'ok'.
[integration] In the booted app, a user with only the member baseline receives 403 with error code permissions from GET /roles.
[integration] In the booted app, a global admin receives 200 from GET /roles.

routing.reasoning: Prescribed Requires metadata, two guard registrations and one existing MCP double adjustment introduce no new authorization algorithm or abstraction; strict TDD remains mandatory for access-control wiring.

modifiedFiles.reason: its module provides `PermissionService` as `{ projectIdsWithKey }` only, and the `RequiresGuard` now on the MCP routes calls `can` for the implicit `mcp.access`, which would throw. The replacing invariant: the double also has `can` resolving `{ allowed: true, reason: 'implicit' }`; every case (409 when MCP is off, 403 for a user principal, initialize, tools/list, tools/call) keeps its expected outcome.

userStories.title: Declare the system writers' catalog keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add validated system-writer metadata to exactly 35 classes representing all 30 system-access catalog keys.

**Motivation** — A deletion that leaves a route without a key, or changes what a role can do, fails CI.

**Approach** — New file `apps/api/src/permissions/system-writer.decorator.ts`:

```ts
import { SetMetadata } from '@nestjs/common';
import { findCatalogEntry } from './catalog';

export const SYSTEM_WRITER_METADATA = 'koda:system-writer';

/**
 * Declares the catalog key of a class that writes on the system's own behalf (a sweeper, a cron
 * processor, an outbox subscriber, a webhook intake). The catalog contract test reads it back.
 * Throws at decoration time unless `key` is a catalog key with access `system`.
 */
export const SystemWriter = (key: string): ClassDecorator => {
  if (findCatalogEntry(key)?.access !== 'system') {
    throw new Error(`@SystemWriter needs a system catalog key, got '${key}'`);
  }
  return SetMetadata(SYSTEM_WRITER_METADATA, key);
};
```

userStories.title: Commit the seeded-role allow/deny matrix
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Freeze real PermissionService decisions for all seeded roles and post-fold catalog keys, independently pinning Appendix A and ownership behavior.

**Motivation** — A seeded role whose entries drift, for example a wildcard that starts matching a new key, changes who may do what with no test failing.

**Approach** — A unit spec, `apps/api/src/permissions/role-matrix.spec.ts`, builds a real `PermissionService` over `InMemoryPermissionStore` (as `permission.service.spec.ts` does), with project `p1` known to the store.
- **One row per seeded role R** (`SYSTEM_ROLES`, 11 roles).
- **The row's principal:**
  - for R = `agent`: an AGENT principal bound to `agent` globally;
  - otherwise: a USER principal (legacy role `MEMBER`) bound to the global `member` baseline, plus R itself — globally when R is a GLOBAL role (`owner`, `admin`), in `p1` when R is a PROJECT role. For R = `member`, the baseline binding alone.

  The baseline is bound explicitly, so the matrix does not depend on `PermissionService`'s no-binding fallback, which drop-legacy removes.
- **One column per catalog key K** (`PERMISSION_CATALOG`, 221 keys).
- **Each cell** is the pair `[can(principal, K, {}).reason, can(principal, K, { projectId: 'p1' }).reason]`. A fresh store and service are built per row, so no cached keys carry between rows.
- **The file.** The matrix is serialised as JSON, with roles in `SYSTEM_ROLES` order and keys in catalog order. It is compared with the committed file `apps/api/src/permissions/__snapshots__/role-matrix.json` through Vitest's file snapshot. A change to the catalog, a seeded role or `PermissionService.can` shows up as a reviewed diff of that file. `bunx vitest run -u` regenerates it.

**Pinned cells.** Taken from Appendix A, not from the file, so the committed matrix is checked against the design at least at these points. `g` is the `global` reason, `p1` the project reason; all were executed against `PermissionService` at `07b11c0a` (with the fold's two `project-admin` keys checked by their pre-fold holders):

| Role | Key | Context | Reason |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `viewer` | `ticket.create` | p1 | `not-granted` |
| `viewer` | `comment.create` | p1 | `granted` |
| `developer` | `ticket.transition.start` | p1 | `granted` |
| `developer` | `ticket.delete` | p1 | `not-granted` |
| `developer` | `comment.update` | p1 | `not-owner` |
| `project-admin` | `member.add` | p1 | `granted` |
| `project-admin` | `role.binding.manage` | p1 | `granted` |
| `project-admin` | `agent.update` | g | `not-granted` |
| `admin` | `role.binding.owner` | g | `not-granted` |
| `owner` | `role.binding.owner` | g | `granted` |
| `agent` | `role.binding.owner` | g | `principal-type` |
| `agent` | `mcp.access` | g | `implicit` |
| `member` | `thread.workspace.create` | g | `granted` |
| `member` | `project.create` | g | `not-granted` |
| `reviewer` | `ticket.transition.close` | p1 | `granted` |
| `triager` | `ticket.transition.reject` | p1 | `granted` |
| `approver` | `approval.decide` | p1 | `granted` |

**Ownership.** The `.own` ACs loop over every cell whose `p1` reason is `not-owner`. `resource.createdBy` is a `PrincipalRef`: the row principal's own ref is `{ type: 'USER', id }` (or `'AGENT'` for the `agent` row); "another principal" is `{ type: 'USER', id: 'someone-else' }`.

Use the real-service wiring from permission.service.spec.ts with a fresh FakeCacheManager and PermissionCache per row; do not mock can or compute expected reasons by reimplementing permission rules. Register each USER with store.addUser(..., 'MEMBER') or AGENT in store.agents, add p1 to store.projects and explicitly bind baselines. Snapshot only the deterministic role -> key -> [global reason, p1 reason] result. Compare the 17 hardcoded expected cells independently of the snapshot. Own-grant cases iterate every not-owner p1 cell; any-row cases iterate OWNABLE_KEYS with a granted p1 cell, including globally granted scope-any keys. This is the binding spec's standalone matrix story, not a separate validation gate.

**Scope** — In: deterministic role-matrix.spec.ts, committed JSON file snapshot, pinned cells and exhaustive ownership assertions. Out: changing the fold (US-001), route/writer declarations (US-002/003/004), checker/collector (US-006/007), seeded role permissions and PermissionService behavior.
- Removing the legacy union and the baseline fallback in `PermissionService`, dropping the legacy tables and columns, deleting `PATCH /agents/:slug/update-roles` and `AGENT_PROJECT_SCOPING` are out of scope (`permissions-p1-drop-legacy`).
- Moving test fixtures from `ProjectMember`, `AgentProject`, `AgentRoleEntry` and `User.role` rows to role bindings is out of scope (`permissions-p1-fixtures-to-bindings`).

**Interface** — Each cell is `[can(principal, K, {}).reason, can(principal, K, { projectId: 'p1' }).reason]`. Ownership inputs use `resource: { createdBy: <PrincipalRef> }`, with `{ type: 'USER', id }` or `{ type: 'AGENT', id }` for self and `{ type: 'USER', id: 'someone-else' }` for other.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] The serialised role matrix equals the committed file apps/api/src/permissions/__snapshots__/role-matrix.json.
[unit] The matrix's role keys equal the SYSTEM_ROLES keys in order (11), and every row's cell keys equal the PERMISSION_CATALOG keys in order (221).

[unit] Reading the 17 pinned cells from the matrix in the design table's order returns ['not-granted', 'granted', 'granted', 'not-granted', 'not-owner', 'granted', 'granted', 'not-granted', 'not-granted', 'granted', 'principal-type', 'implicit', 'granted', 'not-granted', 'granted', 'granted', 'granted'] for viewer/ticket.create/p1, viewer/comment.create/p1, developer/ticket.transition.start/p1, developer/ticket.delete/p1, developer/comment.update/p1, project-admin/member.add/p1, project-admin/role.binding.manage/p1, project-admin/agent.update/global, admin/role.binding.owner/global, owner/role.binding.owner/global, agent/role.binding.owner/global, agent/mcp.access/global, member/thread.workspace.create/global, member/project.create/global, reviewer/ticket.transition.close/p1, triager/ticket.transition.reject/p1 and approver/approval.decide/p1 respectively.
[unit] In every matrix row, the cells for runner.sync and system.outbox.dispatch are ['non-role-key', 'non-role-key'].
[unit] In every matrix row, the health.read cell is ['public', 'public'].
[unit] In every matrix row, every project-scope role key has global reason 'no-project'.
[unit] In every matrix row, no project-scope role key has p1 reason 'no-project'.
[unit] For every row and key whose p1 cell is 'not-owner', can(principal, K, { projectId: 'p1', resource: { createdBy: <the row principal's own ref> } }) returns { allowed: true, reason: 'granted' }.
[unit] For every row and key whose p1 cell is 'not-owner', can with projectId 'p1' and resource.createdBy { type: 'USER', id: 'someone-else' } returns { allowed: false, reason: 'not-owner' }.

[unit] For every row and every key in OWNABLE_KEYS whose p1 cell is 'granted', can with projectId 'p1' and resource.createdBy { type: 'USER', id: 'someone-else' } returns { allowed: true, reason: 'granted' }.

routing.reasoning: Two new files with deterministic but non-trivial role/baseline/ownership fixture construction over a real access-control service; strict security TDD applies to this explicitly bound matrix story.

Existing-code enhancement and security regression safety net, not greenfield. The binding decomposition is exactly US-001 through US-007, including the explicitly specified test-only matrix story. All workdirs remain apps/api even though US-001 also edits the root inventory and regenerates root openapi.json.

Navigation and evidence: codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this session, so discovery used direct Read/Grep/Glob, not an unverified index. The source context was read at .nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:1. Its NestJS/Fastify architecture supersedes the supplied generic Express/Next.js detection; this feature does not touch web. apps/api/package.json:9-29 defines Vitest unit/scoped/DB commands, oxlint and Prisma generation; apps/api/package.json:43-76 confirms Nathapp/Nest 12, platform-fastify and Prisma dependencies. Refused keys throw new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'permissions'). DB fixtures requiring system roles must run SystemRoleSeeder.onApplicationBootstrap() after resetDb, or reset then boot the app. @Requires(keys, { enforcedBy: 'service' }) records the handler/service/route-specific guard's existing check rather than introducing a guard decision. Every guard-enforced route must list RequiresGuard on the class or handler. apps/api/src/permissions/requires.decorator.ts:12-40 defines the metadata with default mode all, default enforcedBy guard, and rejects empty key lists; apps/api/src/permissions/requires.guard.ts:29-59 resolves handler metadata before class metadata, bypasses service enforcement, combines all/any answers, preserves not-owner pass-through and fails closed with permissions. apps/api/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:36-57 is the public-route-plus-RequiresGuard convention to mirror.
